claims.text: The baseline HVAF-i7 process using 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces acceptable coating quality but inadequate coating thickness.
Modifying the HVAF-i7 nozzle and reducing stand-off distance will increase particle velocity.
A spray distance of approximately 300–350 mm is an optimal range for the proposed HVAF-i7 process.
Higher particle velocity will increase deposition efficiency.
Increasing deposition efficiency will overcome the coating-thickness limitation.
Higher particle kinetic energy improves particle impact and flattening into splats.
Improved particle flattening produces a denser coating build-up.
Improved particle impact and splat formation improve coating adhesion.
Higher-velocity particles deform more effectively upon impact.
More effective impact deformation reduces particle rebound.
Increasing particle velocity reduces in-flight oxidation.
The modified process will produce a statistically significant increase in coating thickness relative to the baseline process.
The modified process will maintain minimal oxidation and good adhesion while increasing coating thickness.
The intervention will remain effective when depositing FeCoNiCrAl coatings within internal diameters of approximately 120 mm.
The resulting coating will retain integrity during high-temperature service in an oxidizing atmosphere.

contradictions.description: The proposal simultaneously specifies a 300–350 mm spray distance and deposition within an internal diameter as small as 120 mm, without explaining a torch orientation or nozzle geometry that makes this stand-off distance feasible in that confined geometry.
